# `session_offer_nonexhaustive`: a `match` on an offered label misses a branch

`Chan.offer(ch)` returns the label the peer chose and the channel. A
`match` on that label must have an arm for every branch the protocol offers.
A `match` that leaves one out is this error. It names the missing labels and
lists all of them.

## A program that triggers it

```march
mod Main do
  type Client = Client
  type Server = Server

  protocol Lookup do
    choose by Server:
      ok  -> Server -> Client : Int
      err -> Server -> Client : String
    end
  end

  fn main() do
    let (cc, sc) = Chan.new(Lookup)
    let sc2 = Chan.choose(sc, :ok)
    Chan.close(Chan.send(sc2, 7))
    let (lbl, cc2) = Chan.offer(cc)
    match lbl do
      :ok ->
        let (_n, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
    end
  end
end
```

The peer may choose `:err`, and the `match` has no arm for it.

## The fix

Add an arm for each branch, and use the channel inside each arm:

```march
mod Main do
  type Client = Client
  type Server = Server

  protocol Lookup do
    choose by Server:
      ok  -> Server -> Client : Int
      err -> Server -> Client : String
    end
  end

  fn main() do
    let (cc, sc) = Chan.new(Lookup)
    let sc2 = Chan.choose(sc, :ok)
    Chan.close(Chan.send(sc2, 7))
    let (lbl, cc2) = Chan.offer(cc)
    match lbl do
      :ok ->
        let (_n, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
      :err ->
        let (_msg, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
    end
  end
end
```

## Why the rule exists

The peer decides which branch to take, so the receiver must be ready for
any of them. A missing arm would leave the receiver with nothing to do when
the peer picks that branch. Unlike an ordinary atom `match`, the set of labels
is closed: the protocol lists them all.

See also: [choice: `choose` and `offer`](../session-types.md#choice-choose-and-offer).
